about: Dated periods drawn on the timeline (server/seed/load-periods.js). Entered by hand from the cited documents; each end names who determined it and the document. Recessions are generated from NBER BCDC_spreadsheet_for_website.xlsx (March 2023; still current: the last announcement is the April 2020 trough).

periods.notes: Dated by the National Bureau of Economic Research, a private research organization whose dates are the accepted reference. The recession runs from the month after the peak through the trough.

periods.name: COVID-19 Public Health Emergency
periods.start_by: Department of Health and Human Services
periods.start_source: Determination that a Public Health Emergency Exists, January 31, 2020 (effective January 27, 2020), under section 319 of the Public Health Service Act
periods.end_by: Department of Health and Human Services
periods.end_source: Expired May 11, 2023, at the end of the last 90-day renewal (February 9, 2023); HHS fact sheet of May 9, 2023
periods.notes: Declared by Secretary Alex Azar and renewed every 90 days; the Biden administration announced in January 2023 that it would end on May 11.

periods.name: COVID-19 National Emergency
periods.start_source: Proclamation 9994, March 13, 2020, 85 FR 15337 (the emergency beginning March 1, 2020)
periods.notes: Declared under the National Emergencies Act and the Stafford Act; the first national emergency Congress ended by joint resolution.
